history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is at Bodaganj (Rajganj block), on the banks of the Teesta river, ~20 km from Jalpaiguri town - NOT in Jalpaiguri town. Documented with the corrected location. One of the 51 Shakti Peethas: the left leg (thumb/toe of the left foot) of Goddess Sati is said to have fallen here when Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra dismembered her body. The name Bhramari ('like a bee') comes from the legend that Goddess Parvati took the form of a giant bee (emitting a swarm of bees, hornets and wasps) to slay the demon Arunasura who had driven the gods from heaven. Local lore says the shrine began when a forest-dwelling saint found the stone toe in a pit in the dense Dooars forest, built a thatched shrine, and later installed the eight-armed idol; the hut has since become a red-coloured single-floor concrete temple in traditional Bengali style. Devotees bathe in the Teesta before worship and value the site for tantric sadhana. Local folklore also links the temple to Devi Chaudhurani and her mentor Bhavani Pathak, who are said to have worshipped here. Coordinates from map geocode POI match (Bhramri Devi Mandir, Rajganj, 735218) - approximate, ~18-20 km from Jalpaiguri town, consistent with sources.

name: Bhramari Devi Temple
town: Bodaganj (CSV town 'Jalpaiguri' is WRONG - temple is ~20 km from Jalpaiguri town, on the Teesta)
town_description: Bodaganj is a village in Rajganj block of Jalpaiguri district on the banks of the Teesta river, about 20 km from Jalpaiguri town. Once dense Dooars forest, the area is now rural and agricultural; the temple sits in a quiet forest-edge setting that gives it a raw, non-commercial pilgrimage atmosphere.

travel.road: About 20 km from Jalpaiguri town by road; regular buses and local transport to Bodaganj/Rajganj.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navaratri (Sep-Oct) and Kumbham (Mar-Apr) for the main festivals.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published; the temple stands in a forest area - visitors are advised to arrive before 4:30 PM (verify). Bathe in the Teesta before entering, per custom.
